The present petition has been filed seeking regular bail in connection with FIR No.403/2023 under Section 376 IPC and Section 6 of POCSO Act registered at Police Station Prem Nagar, Delhi.

2. The case of the prosecution is that the victim along with her relative arrived at the Police Station and handed over a written complaint wherein she alleged that her mother had contracted a second marriage with the victim's father, who left her mother as he was suspicious as to her mother's character.
Thereafter, victim's mother along with victim and her two younger brothers moved to the house of accused Ali Akhtar and started living with them.
3. According to the victim, Ali Akhtar had an evil eye on her from the very beginning.
Few days prior to Holi in the year 2023 when no one else was present at home, Ali Akhtar committed forcible sexual assault upon her.
She tried to tell her mother but out of fear she could not disclose the

In the following month, being afraid of Ali Akhtar, victim went to stay at her friend Priya's house, which was situated at Mangal Bazar Road.
She remained there for 10 days.

On the 10th day,
the petitioner, who was engaged to Priya, came there and at that time no one else was present in the house and the petitioner also committed sexual assault upon her.

4. Mr. Rohit Saroj, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the victim got pregnant and the pregnancy was terminated at Hospital and the foetal material was sent for DNA Profiling along with the blood samples of the present petitioner.
5. Mr. Saroj has handed over a compilation across the bar, the same is taken on record.

Referring to Gaurav Kumar vs State Nct Of Delhi on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154745913/
1 the FSL Report in the said compilation, he submits that there is no finding that the DNA of the present petitioner has matched with the DNA of the foetal material.

sentences.text: 6. He submits that no DNA profiling of blood samples of co-accused Ali Akhtar was done.

Further,
the victim made an exculpatory statement before the learned Trial Court in favour of the co-accused Ali Akhtar, on the basis of which learned Trial Court granted bail to co-accused Ali Akhtar.
7. He submits that the allegations against co-accused Ali Akhtar are graver as compared to the present petitioner.

8. He submits that the present petitioner has been made a scapegoat and reading of the FIR itself shows that the main culprit is Ali Akhtar and it is only under the fear of her mother and the said co-accused that the petitioner has been falsely implicated.
9. He contends that the petitioner has clean antecedents, and the petitioner is in custody for the past two and a half years.
10. He further contends that there is a delay of three months in This is a digitally signed order.

11. Per contra, Mr. Ajay Vikram Singh, learned APP for the State has argued on the lines of the Status Report.
12. The reading of the FIR shows that two different incidents have been mentioned in the same FIR.
In the opening part of the FIR, the allegations are essentially against the co-accused Ali Akhtar.
It is also the case of the prosecution that the petitioner was afraid of Ali Akhtar, therefore, she went to stay at her friend Priya's house.
13. The allegations against co-accused Ali Akhtar appears to be graver and more descriptive as compared to the allegations against the petitioner.

Furthermore, the victim's statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. records that the co-accused Ali Akhtar after forcibly sexually assaulting threatened her with dire consequences in the event she spoke about the incident, which is not the case against the present petitioner.

14. Intriguingly, the blood samples of co-accused Ali Akhtar were not sent for DNA profiling and for being compared with the DNA of the foetal material, when blood samples of the petitioner were so sent.
15. The FSL report only refers to the DNA profiling of the petitioner's blood samples and its comparison with the foetal material.
A perusal of the FSL report shows that it does not give any finding with regard to the matching of petitioner's DNA with that of the foetal material.

17.
Furthermore, it is not in dispute that co-accused Ali Akhtar has been granted bail.
The petitioner has been incarcerated for about two and a half years and the testimony of the victim has already been recorded.
18. It is also not the case of the prosecution that the petitioner has any previous involvements.
19. Considering the circumstances in entirety, this Court is of the view that the petitioner has made out a case for grant of regular bail.

Accordingly, the petitioner is admitted to regular bail subject to his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.20,000/- with one surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court/JMFC/Duty JM, further subject to the following conditions:
a) Petitioner shall appear before the Court as and when the matter is taken up for hearing.

b) Petitioner shall provide mobile number to the IO concerned which shall be kept in working condition at all times and he shall not change the mobile number without prior intimation to the Investigating Officer concerned.
c) Petitioner shall not come in contact with the victim/complainant or any or other witnesses.

20. It is clarified that the observations made herein above are only for the limited purpose of deciding the present bail application and the same shall not be construed as an expression of opinion on merits of the case.
21. The petition is disposed of.
22. Copy of the order be forwarded to the concerned Jail Superintendent
